name: States Rulebook
summary: Every situation the interface has to handle, not only the happy path.
check: Throttle the network, go offline, empty the data, send bad input, and screenshot each state.

rules.title: Empty state
rules.text: Before there is any data, explain what this place is for and give one clear action ("Create your first project").

rules.title: Loading state
rules.text: Skeletons that match the final layout, disabled and busy buttons, progress where the duration is known. The wait should look active.

rules.title: Error state
rules.text: Say what happened in plain words and give a way out: retry, go back, contact support. Never only "Something went wrong".

rules.title: Offline state
rules.text: Tell the user they are offline (a small bar), keep already loaded content visible, queue or disable actions that need the network.

rules.title: Slow network
rules.text: Show incremental progress and partial content. A spinner that never changes looks frozen; after a few seconds, say that it is still working.

rules.title: Zero search results
rules.text: Offer a spelling fix, related results, popular items or a way to clear filters. Never a dead end.

rules.title: Permission denied
rules.text: Explain why access is blocked and how to get it ("Ask an admin", "Allow camera in browser settings").

rules.title: Session expiry
rules.text: Save drafts and form input before signing the user out, and restore them after they sign back in.

rules.title: Form validation
rules.text: Errors appear inline at the exact field, in plain words, after the user leaves the field or submits. Focus moves to the first error. Correct tab order, Enter submits, visible focus rings.

rules.title: Success state
rules.text: Confirm completion clearly and offer the next step ("Track your order", "Continue shopping").

rules.title: Stale data says so
rules.text: When data might be old, show when it was last updated and offer a refresh.

rules.title: Partial content
rules.text: When part of a page fails, show what loaded and explain what did not, with a retry for that part only.

rules.title: Concurrent edits
rules.text: When two people can edit the same thing, detect conflicts and let the user choose what to keep instead of silently overwriting.

rules.title: First run
rules.text: The very first visit to a product area has a short orientation or a useful default, which can be skipped and never comes back unasked.

rules.title: Maintenance and rate limits
rules.text: Planned downtime and rate limits get their own friendly page or message with a time when it will work again.

rules.title: Blank screens
rules.text: A page is never empty white while it loads, fails or has no data. Every wait and every failure shows something useful.
